_: The Gradius comparison corpus. ONE file, read by BOTH sides: scen.py drives
the cartridge with it and porttrace.mjs drives the port with it, so the two
cannot drift apart the way two hand-kept copies of a script do.
Every script begins with the same 400-frame boot prefix, which is the one
PROBE.md already characterised: 200 idle frames, START, 190 more. Game mode
reaches 5 at frame 282, the ship's object becomes alive at 283, and the
stage-intro sub-state $1B holds the player frozen until frame ~310. Holds
therefore start at frame 400, clear of all three -- MEASURED at frame 400:
ALIGNMENT: the port does not model the title screen or the attract demo, so
it cannot be booted cold and compared. The comparison SEEDS the port from
the cartridge's own RAM at frame `align` and free-runs from there.
That is the same arrangement NOTES-player.md 11 used for playermodel.py.
It is stated here because it bounds what the comparison proves: everything
BEFORE a scenario's align frame is untested by it. Wave 4 moved that bound:
`intro-boot` aligns at 282, the mode-4 handover, so the stage intro and
everything $9B3E computes ARE compared -- see the `_align` note above.
POKE SYNTAX. `"poke": "0040=6"` holds a value for the whole compared
window; `"poke": "001F=1@+40"` writes it at ONE frame, align+40. Both are
applied at $80B5 -- after the sample -- on BOTH sides, so the first frame
they affect is the next one. Use the one-frame form for any value the
cartridge itself only ever holds for one frame; holding such a value is
testing invented state. See porttrace.mjs POKEABLE and POKEABLE_RANGES
for what may be poked and why each address is allowed -- wave 5 added the
terrain collision map $0500-$06FF, which is the only way in this corpus to
reach $C2C1, the terrain route into the death.
_align: A scenario may override `align`. WAVE 4 ADDED THAT because the port now
models the stage intro, and the intro happens at frames 283-309 of a boot
and 614-640 of a respawn -- i.e. before the corpus's own align of 400.
`intro-boot` aligns at 282, which is the MODE-4 HANDOVER FRAME: $8165 is
`LDA #$00 / STA $1B / INC $00`, three instructions, so the sample at 282
reads mode 5 with $1B = 0 and mode 5's own handler has not run yet. The
first compared frame, 283, is therefore the port running $9B3E itself --
the ship's position, both position rings, $0100, $0120, $35, $3F and $55
are all COMPUTED on the port side rather than seeded, for the first time.
`intro-respawn` aligns at 614, the frame the cartridge's $979D ran, and so
compares intro states 1-4 and the exit but NOT $9B3E. That is not a choice
of coverage: $979D jumps into $9B3E in the SAME frame, and $979D is wave
5. Seeding one frame earlier would put the port on an arm that throws.
_watch: Extra RAM added to probe.lua's state vector through its own --watch
mechanism, so the oracle is EXTENDED without being EDITED. Every address
here is one the port claims to model; nothing is watched for decoration.
The 48 ring bytes are the reason the Option comparison is worth anything:
comparing $0361/$0362 alone would pass for a port that trailed the ship by
the wrong number of ring entries on a straight-line hold.
ADDRESSES WATCHED AHEAD OF THE PORT: there are none left. $19, $24 and $4C
were the last three and wave 4 modelled all three; the mechanism worked as
designed -- they were recorded from the cartridge in wave 1, a wave before
any line existed that had to reproduce them. Use it again for wave 5.
WAVE 2 ADDED THE HUD'S STATE AND ITS INPUTS: $48 (the four-phase rotation,
$88A4 INC $48 -- real port state), and $20/$21 $42 $46 $07E0-$07EA, which
src/hud.js READS and nothing in the port yet WRITES. Watching a seeded
constant proves little on its own; it is here so that the frame waves 5-7
make it move is compared against data recorded now. src/state.js says the
same thing under SEEDED INPUTS, at the code.
WAVE 3 ADDED THE ENEMY POOL AND THE SPAWN ENGINE. Sixteen arrays x the ten
enemy slots 12-21 ($010C-$0115 status, $012C metasprite, $014C anim timer,
$016C anim frame, $018C palette OR, $030C type, $032C/$034C Y, $036C/$038C
X, $03AC carrier, $03BC/$03EC Y velocity, $042C X velocity / explosion
cursor, $040C the shot countdown / $04EC its reload, $046C handler state,
$048C sub-state, $04AC the second phase counter, $04CC unidentified but
cleared by $A527), plus the engine's own zero
WAVE 3'S TEST PASS ADDED THE THREE $A527 ARRAYS THE COMPARISON COULD NOT
SEE. src/enemies.js clearSlot() justifies its reading of the two Y-indexed
stores with 'the watch list compares addresses' -- and for $0460+j
($A52E) and $0480+22+j ($A52B) it did not: neither range was watched, so
dropping either store was green over all 18 scenarios and caught only by
tests/enemies.test.js. $044C-$0455 (the X sub-pixel velocity $B154 adds)
was the one of the twenty-one X-indexed arrays that was missing too.
Watched now: $044C-$0455, $0460-$0469, $0496-$049F. They are constant zero
across this corpus -- that is the POINT: the port must keep them zero, and
wave 6's $BE93 is the first code that will make them move.
WAVE 4 ADDED THE FLOW MACHINE'S OWN BYTES. $09 and $16 (the two gates on
$9ADA that are not $0D), $22-$29 (the four per-player saved bytes $9B62-
$9B74 restores at every intro -- checkpoint, stage, meter, $1A), $33 (the
button-code match counter $9765 walks on EVERY paused frame) and $3B/$3C
(the per-player cheat counts $9AFF tests before running it).
WAVE 5 ADDED $0A, the bitfield of players still in the game. $97C7 reads it
to decide whether the respawn switches players, and $97F9 (the game-over
arm, still a throw) is its only writer -- so like $20 it is a byte the port
READS and never writes. It is 1 in the seed of all 23 scenarios; watching a
constant is worth exactly what src/state.js says under SEEDED INPUTS, and it
is here so the wave that makes it move is judged against data recorded now.
AND IT REMOVED THREE SKIPS. $19, $24 and $4C were watched-but-unmodelled
since wave 1 -- deliberately, so that the wave which had to reproduce them
would be judged against data recorded BEFORE it was written. All three are
modelled now ($9663 tests $19, $9B68 reads $24,X into $3F and $55, $96F6
DECs $4C) and the SKIPPED count in compare.mjs drops from 9 to 6.
$6A:$6B is the one to look at hardest. It is a REAL CPU POINTER into the
ROM's wave lists, and comparing it is what makes the wave-record walk
checkable rather than merely plausible: 00-recon-enemies.md 1 recorded it
stepping $A846 -> $A848 -> ... -> $A858 as each of chunk 0's ten records
fired, and $A85B after the chunk switch at scroll $0200. A port that
abstracted the wave list into an array index could not be held to that.
WAVE 4'S TEST PASS ADDED THE $0700 QUEUE AS AN IMAGE. Until this commit the
only compared byte of the whole page was $0E, its LENGTH: 57 addresses in
page 7 were watched and every one of them was $07A0 or above (the rings and
the score). So the intro's packet COMPOSITION -- the whole of $9BF0 and
$9C12 -- was held by a byte count, and three content mutations that leave
the count alone were MEASURED green on all 21 scenarios: $9C12's three
producers emitted in the wrong order, $9BFD/$9C02's canned packets swapped,
and $9BF5's `$19 + 8` made `+ 9`. $0700-$074F is watched now, 80 bytes, and
porttrace.mjs seeds the same range from the cartridge's own RAM at the align
frame -- the page is NOT rebuilt each frame (a frame whose $0E is 1 leaves
the last frame's bytes sitting behind the cursor), so a port that started it
at zero would differ on every byte past the cursor from frame one.
WHY THE PREFIX STOPS AT $074F, said here rather than left to be found: $0E
never exceeds 40 on an ordinary frame, so 80 bytes covers those whole with
40 bytes of slack behind them. The intro's four-block frames reach 149 and
are compared for their first 80 -- $9BF0's 48 and $9C12's 37 in full, and
about the first two of $9C24's four terrain blocks. A wrong FOURTH block on
an intro frame is NOT caught here; $57/$58/$3E/$54/$55 and
tests/terrain.test.js hold that. $07A0 upward is deliberately not added:
those addresses are the rings and the score, which the port keeps as their
own fields, and watching them through the queue page would compare the
wrong one.
WAVE 6 ADDED THE WEAPON SLOTS AND THE SCORE'S THRESHOLD. Object slots 3-11
-- shot A ($0123-$0125), shot B ($0126-$0128) and the missiles ($0129-
$012B), one per owner (the ship and its two Options) -- across the eight
arrays the firing block, the two movement loops and the sweep touch:
$0103 status ($C0C3 clears it), $0123 the metasprite (0 = SLOT FREE),
$0163 the SUBTYPE (0 shot / 1 laser / 2 the DOUBLE's diagonal / 3 missile),
$0323/$0343 Y, $0363/$0383 X, and $03A3-$03AB, which in THAT slot range is
not the carrier byte but the AUTOFIRE TIMERS ($03A3,X slot A, $03A6,X slot
B). The timers are the reason this range is watched rather than just the
positions: they are FROZEN while a slot is occupied, so the fire cadence is
lifetime + $35, and a port with a fixed 21-frame cadence is only visible
here. Plus $2A/$2B, the extra-life score threshold $84D9 compares against.
WAVE 7 ADDED $17, THE POWER-UP RANK. It is the one byte that couples the
power-ups to enemy behaviour -- 23 readers, thresholds at >= 2 and >= 3 --
and it is NOT wiped by the death ($9B3E clears $3D-$97 and $17 is below
that), so a port that recomputed it anywhere but $9AC4 diverges across every
respawn. `capsule-sweep` drives it 0,1,2,3,4 in one 300-frame window;
MEASURED on the cartridge in that same window, $BBE5 -- the $17 >= 3 consumer
00-plan.md risk 5 names -- ran ZERO times, because $BBC1 jumps the whole
ladder while $19 | $1A is 0. The stage-1 rank consumers that DO run sit behind
$BC59, the enemy-bullet allocator, which is a loud throw.
$42 and $46 are not new to this list -- wave 2 put them here as seeded
constants, deliberately, so that the wave which had to move them would be
judged against data recorded before it existed. This is that wave.
WAVE 8 ADDED THE SOUND DRIVER'S ZERO PAGE. $001C (the BGM de-dupe byte
$839B compares against and $97E9 clears), $00B0-$00FB (the four 17-byte
channel structs at $B0/$C1/$D2/$E3 plus the driver's own scratch, as ONE
range because that is what it is -- $DD/$DE is the TRIANGLE struct's +$B/+$C
reused as the single global sub-phrase return address, $F0-$F3 is the NOISE
struct's +$D..+$10 reused as the fade globals, and $DF/$E0/$E1/$E8 are
$EC1E's scratch sitting on top of the triangle's +$D..+$F and the noise's
+$5), and $01A0-$01B0, where $9AF0 parks pulse 1's whole struct across a
pause and $9B33 restores it.
THIS IS NOT A CONSTANT-FIELD WATCH. The corpus aligns at frame 400 and the
stage-1 BGM has been playing since 310, so the seed hands the port three
channels MID-STREAM -- owners $13/$14/$15, pointers somewhere inside
$F396/$F3B1/$F426, duration counters mid-note -- and it has to stay in phase
for the whole window. $B2 alone changes on its own: the pulse-1 part ends at
game frame 823 (MEASURED, 513 frames of ownership from 310), which is inside
long-idle and enemy-waves.
The four APU/driver work counters (audioTicks, audioChannels, apuWrites,
apuDigest) are NOT watch addresses -- APU registers are write-only and a
--watch cannot read them back. They come from objloop.lua instead, which
counts $ED02 and $ED46 executions and digests every $4000-$400F write.
THE FINAL VERIFICATION PASS (wave 99) ADDED $0200-$02FF, THE SHADOW OAM --
256 addresses, the single largest addition since the corpus was built, and
the one every wave from 5 to 8 wrote down as its biggest blind spot in
almost the same words. Before this the whole of page $02 had ZERO watched
addresses: the display list was held by sprite 0's four bytes (s0y/s0t/
s0a/s0x) and three work counters (msExpanded, spriteRecords, spritesStored),
so a sprite drawn at the wrong OAM SLOT, or with the wrong TILE, ATTRIBUTE
or X, was green everywhere as long as the COUNT was right. The port has
modelled the page all along (state.shadowOam; porttrace.mjs's peek has
mapped $0200-$02FF since it was written) -- nobody had ever asked the
cartridge for it.
MEASURED, and this is why the addition is worth its 256 addresses: with the
slot stride at $8AF2 changed from $C4 to $C0, all four probed scenarios
still reported `all TIER 1 fields exact` while the display list was wrong
in 43,809 places. The same break is caught by the DISPLAY LIST block in
compare.mjs on the first frame.
PAGE $02 IS NOT GRADED FIELD BY FIELD, and compare.mjs explains why at
length above compareDisplayList(): src/oam.js clears shadow OAM to $F4 in
one go, while the cartridge's blank pass $8BAB writes $F4 into the Y BYTE
ONLY of the slots past the cursor and leaves their tile/attribute/X stale.
So hidden slots differ in bytes 1-3 by construction -- 36,244 slot-frames
of it on `idle` alone. What is compared instead is EXACT and is not weaker:
the Y byte of all 64 slots on every frame, and all four bytes of every slot
the CARTRIDGE is actually showing. Corpus total: 786,816 slot-frames,
170,765 of them live, 0 mismatches.
_knownFail: docs/knowledge/01: annotate known-unfixable divergence rather than deleting
the scenario, and make an unexpected PASS fail the run so nobody forgets to
remove the annotation. Each entry names the fields, the mechanism, and the
measurement that established it. Nothing is listed here that has not been
traced to a specific instruction on the cartridge.
THE LIST IS EMPTY, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF WAVE 2. It held exactly one
entry for the port's whole life -- `terrain-streams-at-double-rate`, over
w_000E w_0054 w_0055 w_0057 w_0058 -- and it was removed in the SAME commit
that ported $8898 (src/hud.js), because compare.mjs FAILS on a knownFail
that no longer diverges. Both measured causes are closed:
A ($8641, wave 1) $80B0 appends ONE $00 -- the drainer's mode-0 stop byte
-- on every non-lag frame. Without it w_000E read one low on frame 401,
the FIRST compared frame.
B ($8898, wave 2) the HUD tick shares the terrain streamer's $0E gate and
runs seven bytes above it ($9AC7 vs $9ACE), producing 8/14/39 bytes on
ODD $02 frames. Measured: entered 390, past both gates 195, even 0 and
odd 195; build histogram {0:196, 1:195} on the cartridge against
{0:1, 1:390} on the port; and starving the cartridge's own gate turned
it INTO the port while both sides still emitted the same 140 blocks.
So the divergence was a phase error in $54/$55/$57/$58/$0E, never a content
error in VRAM. Those five fields are TIER 1 again. If one of them starts
diverging that is a REGRESSION in src/hud.js or src/terrain.js -- do not
re-annotate it here without a fresh measurement of its own.
_expectDying: How many frames of a scenario's COMPARED WINDOW the CARTRIDGE spends with
$0100 >= 2, i.e. dying. Optional; compare.mjs's DEATH COVERAGE block fails
the run when a scenario that carries one no longer matches it.
WHY IT EXISTS. terrain-death and terrain-death-miss kill (and deliberately
fail to kill) by poking ONE collision-map cell, and which cell that is
depends on the camera at the poke frame -- kill.py derives $05B3 from
playerX 80, playerY 96 and $3E = 93. Change the script, the align frame or
the scroll rate and the poke lands where the ship is not: NOTHING fails.
Neither side dies, both sides still agree frame for frame, and the summary
still reads `0 failures` while terrain-death has quietly become a second
copy of terrain-death-miss. docs/knowledge/03's first shape exactly.
MEASURED (node tools/oracle/compare.mjs, this commit): 823 dying frames
across 7 of the 23 scenarios -- terrain-death 121 (first at f501),
right-wall 121 (f493), diag-rd-lu 107 (f533), diag-ru-ld 121 (f445),
lr-both 121 (f482), speed6-right 121 (f515), speed3-diag 111 (f529).
terrain-death-miss carries an EXPLICIT 0: the control is as load-bearing as
the kill, because it is what proves the poke is what does the killing.
The number comes off the ORACLE artifact, never the port, so a port that
cannot die is unable to satisfy it by agreeing with itself.
SEEN RED: changing terrain-death's poke to the miss cell 05B4 and
re-recording ->  [FAIL] terrain-death 0 dying frames, expected 121, while
every field comparison stayed green (0 failures).

scenarios.name: intro-boot
scenarios.why:
THE STAGE INTRO, driven rather than seeded. Aligned at 282 -- the frame mode 4's three instructions ($8165 LDA #$00 / STA $1B / INC $00) hand mode 5 a $1B of 0 -- so the FIRST compared frame, 283, is the port executing $9B3E: the $3D-$97 wipe, the $0100/$0300/$0500-$06FF page clears, the per-player restore ($22->$42, $24->$3F and $55, $26->$19, $28->$1A), $882C's RAM side effects, and the start position out of $9BD4[$9BCC[$19] + ($3F>>1)]. Everything the other 18 scenarios take from the cartridge's RAM at align 400, this one computes.

MEASURED with flowprobe.py on this exact script's boot prefix: $9B3E@283, $9BF0@284, $9C12@285, $9C1E@286, $9C24 on 287-309 (23 frames, 4 x $9D8E on each of 287-308 = 88 calls), $9C3C@309, first $982A@310. $0E reads 1, 49, 37, 40, then 149 for twenty-one frames (287-307: 308 is the frame all four $9D8E calls are throttled and $0E falls to 1, and 309 is the exit) -- the four ungated blocks plus $8641's terminator. $0D reads 6,3,3,3 then 5 for twenty-three frames then 4,3,2,1,0, and the sprite-0 split first fires on 314, the frame it reaches 0.

THE ONE LAG FRAME IN THE WHOLE CORPUS IS INSIDE THIS WINDOW. $882C writes 2304 bytes to $2007 in one NMI (h_8871 = 6 chunks, h_888B = 2304) and the frame overruns: probe.lua and objloop.lua both record lag.dropAtGameFrame = 283, and the same script with a death records 283 AND 614. It is attributed to the frame that was still running, so it belongs on row 283 -- which is what src/flow.js fullScreenLoad() reproduces and what makes `lagged` a field with teeth for the first time.
scenarios._: 240 idle frames after the boot prefix rather than 60: the tail is 325 frames of ordinary play whose ENTIRE state came from the port's own intro, so an error in anything $9B3E computes has 325 frames to show itself instead of being absorbed by the next seed.

scenarios.name: intro-respawn
scenarios.why:
THE SECOND INTRO, which is the same five states reached from a completely different place: the ship dies at f493 ($C1D6, measured once), $96EF counts $4C from 120 down over f494-f613, and $979D runs on f614 and jumps into $9B3E in the SAME frame. Aligned at 614 because $979D is wave 5 -- seeding one frame earlier would put the port on the arm that throws.

So this compares intro states 1-4 and the exit, from a cartridge state the boot window cannot produce: lives already decremented to 2, the camera reset from 150 to 0, $5E cleared, and the queue starting from $0E = 1 after $882C. MEASURED: $1B steps 1,2,3,4 on 614-617, $9C24 runs on 618-640, $57 goes 0->1 on 639, $1B -> $80 on 640, and $0E is 1,49,37,40,149x21 (618-638) exactly as on the boot.

WHAT IT SETTLES. The plan carried 'respawn = 26 frames, boot = 28, so the exit is data-dependent'. Both are 27 mode-5 frames, measured twice each. The exit IS data-dependent -- $9C24 reads $57 and there is no counter anywhere -- but it lands on the same number every time because $9B3E sets $3F and $55 from the SAME byte and clears $3E/$54/$58, so the streamer's 16-bit lead is exactly 0 at every intro whatever the checkpoint. A 23-frame counter would pass both of these windows; tests/flow.test.js is what separates the two models, by starting the phase with a non-zero lead.

scenarios.name: pause
scenarios.why:
PAUSE, START-pressed at game frame 450 and again at 500 -- the same two frames 00-recon-flow.md 8 measured, replayed as a per-frame comparison instead of a transition list. $9ADA toggles $15 on a START EDGE ($05, not $07) when $1B is $80-$8F and $09/$16/$0D are all 0; $9650's first branch then jumps the whole update to $9A8C, past the spawn engine, the enemy-bullet engine, THE PLAYER, the enemy update and the $3E->$12 scroll latch.

What the window has to show, on both sides: $15 0->1 at 450 and 1->0 at 500; the camera $3D/$3E/$3F and the latched $12 frozen for exactly those 50 frames while $54/$55/$57/$58 keep moving (the streamer is PAST the pause jump and still runs); $0120/$0140/$0160 frozen (no player, no ring); the enemy slots frozen; and the split still running, because $15 skips $9AA0 and lands ON $9AA3.

This is the scenario wave 1's knownFail was waiting for: the port gated only advanceCamera() on $15 and so kept flying the ship while paused, and no scenario in the corpus could see it because nothing wrote $15.

scenarios.name: terrain-death
scenarios.why:
TERRAIN DEATH, BY POKE -- and the only scenario in the corpus that reaches $C2C1, one of the four routes into $C1D6. It has to be poked: 00-recon-terrain.md measured stage 1's pages 0-3 as containing ZERO solid tile bits and nothing here gets past camera page 0, so $C3A3 returns 0 on all 242 of its calls in every other scenario and the whole terrain arm ($C2A5/$C2B5/$C2BC/$C2C1) is reached, checked, and never true.

The cell is $05B3 and it did NOT come from src/terrain.js. kill.lua re-implements $C3D3 independently and kill.py drove THIS script through the cartridge three ways:
  python games/gradius/tools/oracle/kill.py --frames 640 \
      --script "200:,10:S,190:,240:" --at 500
    mode=none  poked=[]        $C2C1: 0        $1B == $A0 first at: None
    mode=hit   poked=[0x5b3]   $C2C1: [501]    $1B == $A0 first at: 501
    mode=miss  poked=[0x5b4]   $C2C1: 0        $1B == $A0 first at: None
    at the poke frame: playerX=80 playerY=96 page=5 idx=179 shift=4
$10 is bits 4-5 of the cell, which is the field $C402/$C409 select for tile row 14 -- the row the ship's own Y of 96 lands in. So a port whose index arithmetic is off by ANYTHING reads a different byte, sees 0 and flies on, and w_0100/w_001B/w_004C diverge from frame 501.

What the window then compares, on both sides: the death ($0100 1 -> 2, $1B $80 -> $A0, $4C 0 -> 120, $0140 and $0160 zeroed by $C1D6), the $C0FA explosion walk over $0120/$0140/$0160 for 120 frames INCLUDING the $0140 that goes to 255 at the table's $00, the $96EF countdown, and $979D's respawn at frame 622 running $9B3E in the same frame -- lives 3 -> 2, the camera reset and one dropped NMI from $882C. Frames 622-639 are the intro.

scenarios.name: terrain-death-miss
scenarios.why:
THE MISS CONTROL for terrain-death, and it is the reason that scenario is worth anything. Identical script, identical poke frame, ONE BLOCK ROW LOWER: $05B4 instead of $05B3, and $FF rather than $10 so it is not the value that saves it either. $C3F3's `LSR / LSR / CLC / ADC $A0` means +1 on the cell index is +4 on the tile row, i.e. 32 px down the screen from a ship that is not moving.

MEASURED on the cartridge (kill.py mode=miss, above): $C2C1 never fires and $1B never reaches $A0 in 640 frames. So this window must be byte-identical to `idle` and the ship must live to the end. Without it, `terrain-death` is satisfied by a port that dies whenever ANY byte of the map is set -- which is docs/knowledge/03's first shape wearing a poke.

scenarios.name: enemy-waves
scenarios.why:
THE ENEMY SCENARIO. 1465 compared frames -- long enough for all ten of stage 1's chunk-0 wave records (fired at game frames 378 before the align, then 506, 634, 762, 890, 954, 1018, 1082, 1146, 1210), the $FF terminator, the CHUNK SWITCH at scroll $0200 (frame 1339, cursor $A858 -> $A85B), and chunk 1's first four records. Three enemy types are dispatched in the window: $05/$85 the fan ($B0AF, 4840 dispatches), $08/$88 the wavy one ($B26C, 3954) and $04/$84 the arc ($B205, 570, first at frame 1722). It also covers one natural ALLOCATION FAILURE at frame 1152, which is the behaviour that drops a member and collapses a squadron's spacing.

WHY RD, AND WHY IT IS THE ONLY CHOICE. Without weapons the ship cannot kill anything, and every enemy in stage 1's opening homes on the player's Y, so it dies -- MEASURED, first death frame per 1460-frame hold: idle 1051, R 493, RU 445, U 1076, L ~1180. compare.mjs truncates at the death, and a death also RESETS THE CAMERA at the respawn (measured: after the L-run's death the spawn engine re-fired chunk 0's first record at scroll $0020, frame 1299), so the chunk switch never happens. RD parks the ship in the bottom-right corner at (240,192), where the fan's return leg and the wavy one's approach both miss: it survives to frame 1865 and dies at 1866, which is where this scenario stops. Nothing else in the corpus reaches past frame 640.

The cartridge's one lag frame in this run is at game frame 283, i.e. before the align -- so romLagInWindow is 0 and the lag comparison still has teeth via long-idle.

scenarios.name: fade-music
scenarios.why:
THE MUSIC FADE, injected for exactly ONE frame (game 400) into the same zero-load window `long-idle` already runs. Added because THREE deliberate mutations inside the fade arm passed all 35 scenarios and 11,695 frames: $EEF0's $F2 clamp as $0C and as $0A, and $ED2C's triangle-kill threshold as 8.

THE CARTRIDGE SETS $F0 ITSELF and this is not a hypothetical value -- MEASURED off enemy-waves' own recorded rows (w_00F0..w_00F3, no poke): f1849 (0,0,0,0), f1850 (1,0,0,0) as $8398 INC $F0 fires IN PLAY, f1855 (1,5,0,15) as the $EEE6 pulse-2 arm runs, f1865 (1,15,0,15) -- and then the run ENDS, because the ship dies at 1866 and compare.mjs truncates there. $F1 needs 48 ticks to move $F2 once, so the corpus sees 16 frames of a ~530-frame fade and nothing downstream of it. No better script exists: the corpus's own first-death measurements are idle 1051, R 493, RU 445, U 1076, L ~1180, and RD -- the hold that survives longest -- IS enemy-waves.

ONE FRAME because $F0 is a LATCH: $8394 BNE $839A stops $8398 running twice and only $EC95 (a request that targets pulse 2) clears it. A held poke would be re-arming something the cartridge arms once, which is invented state.

WHAT THE WINDOW MUST SHOW, on both sides: $F1 counting to $30 and wrapping every 48 frames (f448 496 544 ...), $F2 stepping with it, the TRIANGLE killed outright once pulse 2's faded volume $F3 falls below 7 ($ED32 STA $D4 -- and $D4 IS $D2 + 2, the triangle's own owner byte), and $F2 held at $0B from f928: $ED26 INCs it without a bound and only $EEF4 pulls it back, so the settled behaviour is an 11<->12 oscillation and $0D is never reached. Everything else in the window is `long-idle` byte for byte, which is what makes any divergence attributable to the fade.

scenarios.name: long-idle
scenarios.why: The same zero-load baseline, run for 600 frames instead of 240. Added for one reason and it is stated: the 240-frame scenarios contain three natural lag frames and every one of them falls AFTER its scenario's death truncation, so `lagged` was a compared field that could not fail on any live window. A longer live run is the only way to make the cartridge's own timing part of the comparison rather than a footnote.

scenarios.name: s0-handover
scenarios.why: THE SPRITE-0 HANDOVER, injected for exactly ONE frame (game 440). Added because two agents independently deleted `state.zp1E !== 0` and `state.zp1F !== 0` from the split gate in src/nmi.js and got byte-identical output from all 16 other scenarios: $1E = 1 and $1F = 2 on every one of their 3341 compared frames, so both terms of $9A8C/$9A90 were unfalsifiable -- docs/knowledge/03's third shape. $9C38 (`A9 01 85 1F`) is the cartridge writing this value itself, during the stage intro, which is before align 400; the port produces it there too since wave 4 (see `intro-boot`), and this scenario injects it into a MID-PLAY window instead, where nothing else can. It is ONE frame because $8B1A-$8B2B promotes 1 to 2 on the next build, so a held 1 is a state the cartridge is never in. What the frame after the poke must show, on BOTH sides: $1F 1 -> 2, $1E still 0, the LIVE sprite-0 record in OAM, NO split, and the camera $3D/$3E/$3F held for that one frame because $9A8E branches past $9AA0 as well as past the split.
scenarios._: Idle rather than moving on purpose: the ONLY difference between this scenario and `idle` is the one poked frame, so any divergence is that frame's or its consequences and cannot be confused with a player-input effect.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.why: Nothing held. The zero-load baseline NOTES-lag.md experiment 1 asks for, and the one scenario in which the position ring must NOT advance ($A082: AND #$0F, no direction -> the whole Option chain freezes). A port that advanced the ring every frame passes every moving scenario and fails only this one.

scenarios.name: right-wall
scenarios.why: 80 -> 240 at 1 px/frame takes 160 frames, then 80 more frames sitting on the $A028 CMP #$F0 clamp. The tail is the point: there is NO pre-check on X, so at the wall the integer is re-clamped every frame while $0380 keeps accumulating.

scenarios.name: left-wall
scenarios.why: 80 -> 16 in 64 frames, then 176 frames on the $A03A CMP #$10 clamp. Long tail because the X sub-pixel byte $0380 keeps moving there and a port that freezes it drifts only slowly.

scenarios.name: up-wall
scenarios.why: 96 -> 16 in 80 frames, then 160 on the ceiling. UP's pre-check is $A06E BCC, i.e. it blocks only BELOW $10 -- so UP still RUNS at Y == $10 and still moves $0340. The asymmetry with DOWN is only visible here.

scenarios.name: down-wall
scenarios.why: 96 -> 192 in 96 frames, then 144 on the floor. DOWN's pre-check is $A054 BCS, which blocks AT $C0: at the floor DOWN writes nothing at all -- not the integer, not $0340, not the tilt -- and falls through into the UP test.

scenarios.name: diag-rd-lu
scenarios.why: Two of the four diagonals. There is no diagonal arm in $9FFC: X is done, then Y is done, with the SAME $99:$98 step, so a diagonal covers step*sqrt(2). A port that normalised diagonal speed diverges here and nowhere else.

scenarios.name: diag-ru-ld
scenarios.why: The other two diagonals, so all four are covered and the tilt latch is driven by both nose-up and nose-down inside one run.

scenarios.name: corner-br
scenarios.why: Into the bottom-right corner and then let go. Both clamps at once, and the 40 idle frames at the end check that the ring stops advancing while the ship is parked somewhere other than its start position.

scenarios.name: corner-tl
scenarios.why: Into the top-left corner, the other pair of clamps, with the UP-at-the-ceiling asymmetry active for 120 of the 200 frames.

scenarios.name: lr-both
scenarios.why: $A031 is a FALL-THROUGH target, not an else. LEFT+RIGHT runs BOTH arms: add, clamp, subtract, clamp. Away from a wall the net displacement is zero -- but the ring still advances, because $A082 tests AND #$0F and does not care that the ship did not move.

scenarios.name: ud-both
scenarios.why: UP+DOWN. DOWN is tested first so it normally wins, but the 100 DOWN frames park the ship on the floor first, where DOWN's pre-check declines and UP is honoured instead. A port that gave DOWN unconditional priority is green for the first 100 frames and red after.

scenarios.name: speed6-right
scenarios.why: SPEED level 6, i.e. step = min(6+2,16)*128 = $0400 = 4.0 px/frame. ADDED BECAUSE THE BUTTON-ONLY CORPUS WAS BLIND: $40 reads 0 on every frame the cartridge produces from a script, so `step` is exactly $0100, the low byte is zero, and both sub-pixel accumulators stay 0 forever. A mutation that deleted the fraction add from $A285 altogether left the comparison GREEN over 2,860 frames. $40 = 6 is a level the cartridge itself reaches ($89A1 INC $40) and it makes $0380 move on every frame.

scenarios.name: speed3-diag
scenarios.why: SPEED level 3: step = 5*128 = $0280, so the fraction byte is $80 and CARRIES every second frame. That is the case that separates a real 16-bit accumulator from an integer one -- an integer port is right on half the frames, which is exactly how this class of bug survives. Diagonal, so both $0340 and $0380 carry independently.

scenarios.name: opt2-wiggle
scenarios.why: TWO OPTIONS. $45 is 0 in every button-only scenario, so $A0C8's loop (LDX $45 / DEX / BMI) never executes a single iteration and $0121/$0122/$0141/$0142 are 0 on every compared frame -- the Options track the player but are never DRAWN. With $45 = 2 the loop runs, the Options get metasprite ids 4 and 5 alternating every 8 frames, and they enter the display list.

scenarios.name: wiggle
scenarios.why: Taps and gaps. The tilt latch only samples $9B every 8 frames ($A0BA CMP #$08), so short holds and the gaps between them are the only thing that exercises which frame the latch lands on; and the ring's stop/start is what makes the Option lag a lag in RING ENTRIES rather than in frames.

scenarios.name: autofire-normal
scenarios.why: AUTOFIRE, $44 = 0. A held from game frame 400 for 600 frames, which is the whole of the firing block, both movement loops and the kill chain in one window. MEASURED on the cartridge with exec hooks before the scenario existed: $A235 (slot A spawns) 14, $A250 (slot B) 14, $BE93 (kills) 11 with the first at f494, $AEC1 (a capsule promotion) 0, $C1AF (the wave-7 pickup) 0, $C1D6 0. The poke is a NO-OP -- $44 is already 0 -- and is written down so that the three autofire scenarios differ in exactly one character, which is what makes them each other's controls. What this window pins that no other scenario can: the FROZEN timers ($03A3/$03A6 watched per frame; the measured spawn gaps interleave 21 and 23 and drop to 21 when a shot dies early), the score ($07E4 stepping $10 per kill through src/score.js) and the row-29 digits $892C draws from it.

scenarios.name: autofire-laser
scenarios.why: AUTOFIRE, $44 = 1 (LASER) -- and the only scenario in the corpus that drops a POWER-UP CAPSULE. The laser SURVIVES its own hit ($C0AE CMP #$01 / BEQ $C0C6 returns without $C0B7's free), so one shot sweeps all ten enemy slots and keeps flying: MEASURED 18 kills where $44 = 0 gets 11 in the same window, 4 squadrons cleared ($BEB5, the $0048+$49 counter reaching 0) and 4 capsule promotions ($AEC1), the first at f527. THE SCRIPT'S 60 FRAMES OF DOWN ARE NOT DECORATION: with A alone the ship TOUCHES the first capsule at f626 -- f626 being this probe's own number, poked from f390; the capsule scenarios poke $44 from the align at 400 and the same capsule lands ten frames later, at f647. That contact is $C1AF, PORTED as of wave 7 (src/collision.js, src/powerup.js $894B), so it would collect rather than throw today; the 60 frames of DOWN stay because this scenario is the autofire/laser witness and a pickup inside its window would move $42 and the meter cursor as well. Dropping 60 px moves the first touch to f983, outside this 540-frame window. Measured both ways with flowprobe.py --poke 0044=1@390-1000.

scenarios.name: autofire-double
scenarios.why: AUTOFIRE, $44 = 2 (DOUBLE) -- the only value of $44 for which slot B fires on the SAME frame as slot A ($A128 BEQ $A134 falls into the slot-B block instead of jumping past it), and the only one that puts subtype 2 in a shot slot: `y -= 4` then `x += 4`, dying at y < $10 as well as at x >= $F8. MEASURED: 15 kills from f452 and one capsule promotion at f557. THE 40 FRAMES OF DOWN ARE NOT DECORATION: the capsule it drops is at y = 98 and drifts left from x = 125 at f513 towards a ship parked at (80, 96), and MEASURED on the cartridge it is COLLECTED at f594 -- $42 steps 0 -> 1 -- which is $C1AF, the wave-7 pickup, and a loud throw. Dropping 40 px takes the ship out of the capsule's 16 x 16 box before it arrives. Every shot spawn requests sfx $A0E6[2] = $01, so this scenario is also the one where the port records TWO sound requests in one frame.

scenarios.name: autofire-die
scenarios.why: FIRING INTO THE DEATH: the `right-wall` script with A held. The ship still dies at f493 (MEASURED: $C1D6 fires twice over 600 frames of `RA` and the first is 493, exactly as without A -- moving right, the shots never connect, $BE93 = 0), and the point is the 120 frames after it. `$9FFC LDA $0100 / CMP #$02 / BCC $A006 / JMP $A16F` lands PAST the firing block and INSIDE the movement loops, so the shots already in the air keep flying and keep freeing their slots at x >= $F8 while the wreck explodes -- and then the respawn's $9B3E page clear takes the slots away. A port that gated the whole of $9FFC on $0100 diverges on $0123-$012B for 120 frames.

scenarios.name: autofire-missile
scenarios.why: MISSILES, $41 = 1. The gate is `$41 != 0` AND the slot free AND A HELD (not the edge) with NO timer at all, so the rate limit is purely flight time. The script drives the ship to the floor over its first 120 frames and then holds A there, which is the case a port gets wrong by default: with the ship clamped at Y = $C0 the missile is born at $C6, `$A1AF ADC $A1A4,Y` makes it $C8 on the SAME frame, and `$A1B9 CMP #$C8 / BCS` kills it before it is ever drawn -- so $A26B runs again next frame, silently, for as long as A is held. The fly path itself is `y += 2, x += 0.5` per frame ($0383 alternating $80/$00), and the missile makes NO sound where every shot makes one.

scenarios.name: missile-wall
scenarios.why:
THE MISSILE AGAINST A WALL, BY POKE -- the only scenario in the corpus that reaches $A199, and the reason it has to be poked is the same reason `terrain-death` is: stage 1's pages 0-3 hold zero solid tile bits and nothing here gets past camera page 0, so every terrain probe in every other scenario returns 0 and the missile's whole wall/crawl discrimination ($A18B-$A19C) has never executed on this machine. Wave 6 shipped `freeMissile()` in that arm and BOTH of its offsets unexercised; wave 6's QA measured that swapping them, or deleting the free, was green on all 28 scenarios. 

THE GEOMETRY, and it is the whole scenario. The script is `autofire-missile`'s, so the ship is parked on the floor clamp at (80, $C0) and $A26B re-fires a born-dead missile at ($50, $C6) every frame. $C3AF probes it at Y + 4 = $CA ($C3B7 CPX #$06 sets the carry, so the ADC #$03 adds four), and $A18B probes AGAIN 8 right and 8 up, at ($58, $C2). $C3E9's `tileRow = (Y + $14) >> 3` puts $CA in row 27 and both $C2 and the SHIP's own $C0 in row 26, and $C3F3's `tileRow >> 2` puts rows 24-27 in ONE cell byte. So the missile's first probe and the ship's probe read the SAME BYTE in different 2-bit fields -- field 3 and field 2 -- and the second probe reads the byte eight columns on, in field 2. 

Hence the two pokes. $05EE = $40 is field 3 SET and field 2 CLEAR: the missile's first probe is non-zero and the ship does NOT die at $C2C1. $05F6 = $10 is field 2 of the column eight px right: the second probe is non-zero too, so $A199's BNE takes the WALL arm at $A1D6 and not the $A19E crawl (which is a loud throw in the port -- reaching it would abort the run, and that is the hazard this scenario is threading). The value is 1 and not 2 on purpose: field 2 = 2 is $C2DC, the unported wall break, and the six shot slots probe field 2 of their own column on the same frame. 

WHICH FRAME, and why +210 rather than a round number: $3E advances half a pixel per frame, so a fixed cell index is only under the ship for 16 frames. $3E = 144..151 puts the probe on $05EE, i.e. game frames 601-616; the poke is written at $80B5 AFTER frame align+210 = 610 is sampled, so the affected frame is 611 and BOTH 610 and 611 sit inside that range -- the scenario does not depend on which of the two the harness means. 

WHAT GOES RED. $A1D6 frees the missile BEFORE $A1AF's fly step, so w_0329 reads $C6 = 198 on the affected frame where every other frame of this window reads $C8 = 200 (the missile that stepped into the floor test). One field, one frame, and it is the arm. `missile-wall-miss` is the control.

scenarios.name: capsule-pickup
scenarios.why:
THE NATURAL PICKUP. $44 = 1 (laser) so the kills come fast enough to drop a capsule inside a 300-frame window, and B is NOT held, so $42 survives to the sample point and the meter cursor lands on the bar.

MEASURED, from this scenario's own recorded artifact (out/scen/capsule-pickup.json, transitions of the watched bytes): $47 0 -> 1 at f530 (the first capsule promoted, $AEC1) and 1 -> 2 at f678 (a SECOND squadron); seven kills score $0010 each at f487, 490, 508, 511, 614, 635, 639; and at f647 $42 steps 0 -> 1 while $07E4 goes $70 -> $20 with $07E5 0 -> 1, i.e. $0070 + $0050 -> $0120. One pickup, +$0050, in a window that ends at f699 with $42 still 1.

The recon's own reproduction of this capsule lands at f626 rather than f647, and the difference is not noise: it poked $44 from frame 390 and the corpus pokes it from the align at 400, so ten frames of laser fire move every kill. The artifact is the authority for this scenario.

WHAT IT PINS THAT NOTHING ELSE DOES. $8A30's cursor patch, `$0700[$0E - (8 - $42)] = $55`. Until this scenario $42 was 0 on every compared frame of the corpus, so `LDA $42 / BEQ $8A4B` returned before writing anything and the whole body of the patch was unfalsifiable through the oracle -- the same shape as the sub-pixel accumulator before speed6-right. With $42 = 1 the attribute byte is written on every $89E3 phase, i.e. every 8 frames, and it is compared through w_0700-w_074F.

THE SECOND SQUADRON IS DELIBERATE (00-plan.md's own test focus): $47 steps to 2 inside the window, so the every-16th counter and the $49 group alternation are live state here rather than constants.

scenarios.name: capsule-consume
scenarios.why:
THE SAME CAPSULE, WITH B HELD -- and the two scenarios differ in one character of the script. $9A70's pickup INCs $42 and $9A73's apply consumes it three instructions later, in the same frame, so the power-up lands on the TOUCH FRAME and $42 is never observably non-zero at all.

MEASURED, the two artifacts side by side. Every watched transition in the two windows is identical -- $44 and $17 at f401, $47 at f530 and f678, the seven scoring kills, and the +$0050 at f647 -- EXCEPT the one frame that matters:
  capsule-pickup   f647  w_0042 0 -> 1     w_0040 stays 0
  capsule-consume  f647  w_0042 stays 0    w_0040 0 -> 1
Holding B perturbs nothing else. That is a controlled pair on one capsule, not two runs that happen to differ.

THIS IS THE HELD-VS-EDGE DISCRIMINATOR. $8974 reads $07,X, not $05,X. With B down continuously from frame 400 an EDGE port fires once, at f401, where $42 is 0 and jt_8989[0] is an RTS -- so it would never consume anything and this window would read $42 = 1 and $40 = 0, i.e. it would become a second copy of `capsule-pickup`. The pair is what makes that a failure instead of a coin flip.

The recon proved the same thing the other way round, with a poke rather than a capsule: $42 forced to 1 on EVERY frame with B held drove $40 up by one PER FRAME, 22 increments in 21 frames (00-recon-powerups.md 3). An edge port moves it once.

scenarios.name: capsule-sweep
scenarios.why:
ALL SIX ARMS OF jt_8989 AND EVERY ONE OF THEIR REFUSALS, in one window, with B held throughout. Thirteen ONE-FRAME pokes of $42 (six first-times, six already-owned repeats, and a second SPEED UP at the end); a held poke would be invented state, because $9A73 clears $42 on the very next frame.

MEASURED ON THE CARTRIDGE, this exact script and these exact pokes, before a line of src/powerup.js was written -- and reproduced transition for transition by the recorded artifact:
  f421 $40 0->1                 SPEED UP
  f441 $41 0->1                 MISSILE
  f461 $42 0->2, HELD to f480   MISSILE refused -- THE CAPSULE IS KEPT
  f481 $42 2->0, $44 0->2, $17 0->1   DOUBLE
  f501 $42 0->3, HELD to f520   DOUBLE refused
  f521 $42 3->0, $44 2->1       LASER, applied OVER an owned DOUBLE
  f541 $42 0->4, HELD to f560   LASER refused
  f561 $42 4->0, $45 0->1, $17 1->2   OPTION
  f581 $45 1->2, $17 2->3       OPTION again -- the cap is `>= 2`, so 1 still applies
  f601 $42 0->5, HELD to f620   OPTION refused
  f621 $42 5->0, $46 0->5, $17 3->4   SHIELD
  f641 $42 0->6, HELD to f660   SHIELD refused
  f661 $42 6->0, $40 1->2       SPEED UP AGAIN: no owned test and no cap
with $8974 n=410, $8983 n=402, $89AF/$89BB/$89CF/$8997 n=21 each and $89D3 n=22 -- one apply plus twenty refusals per arm.

THE REFUSALS ARE THE ONLY WAY $42 IS EVER SEEN. Every APPLY clears it inside the frame, so w_0042 shows nothing; every REFUSAL keeps it, so w_0042 holds 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 for twenty frames each and five of the six meter cells get their $8A30 cursor written. A port that consumed the capsule on a refusal is red on w_0042 twenty frames running, five times over.

AND IT IS THE RANK SCENARIO. $17 walks 0,1,2,3,4 -- the whole of what stage 1 can reach -- crossing BOTH thresholds ($BD5F/$BDB3 at >= 2, $BCB8/$BBE5 at >= 3). MEASURED in this same window: $BBE5 n=0 (00-plan.md risk 5, answered by intervention rather than by argument -- $BBC1 jumps the whole ladder while $19 | $1A is 0), $BC59 n=0 (no enemy bullets, so the rank consumers that ARE live on stage 1 are not reached either), $C1C1 n=0 and $C1D6 n=0. The shield from f621 also puts $8B86's force-field metasprite in the display list on every frame after it, which moves msExpanded/spriteRecords/spritesStored -- three compared work counters -- and $45 = 2 from f581 draws two Options, so the OAM order changes twice inside one window.

scenarios.name: capsule-shield
scenarios.why:
THE SHIELD, FIVE HITS AND THE SIXTH KILLS -- `right-wall`'s script with $46 poked to 5 for one frame at the align. The poke is one frame because the cartridge writes 5 once ($899D) and only ever DECs it after; holding it would make an infinite shield, which is a state no cartridge frame is in.

MEASURED, this scenario's own artifact:
  f401  $46 0 -> 5 (the poke), $17 0 -> 1
  f493  5 -> 4   <- the very contact that KILLS the ship in `right-wall`
  f509  4 -> 3     f526  3 -> 2     f542  2 -> 1     f647  1 -> 0, $17 1 -> 0
  f658  $0100 1 -> 2 and $1B $80 -> $A0: the SIXTH contact, and the death
  f779  $979D/$9B3E, the respawn -- 121 dying frames, and the corpus's second lag frame
and the recon reached the same five-then-die shape from a different script and a different tool ($C1BD n=6, $C1C1 n=5, $C1D0 n=5, $BE93 n=5, $8B79 n=105, $8B86 n=247).

`right-wall` IS ITS CONTROL. Same script, same first contact frame, and the only difference is one poked byte: without the shield the ship dies at f493, with it the ship dies at f658. Nothing else in the corpus separates "absorbed" from "immune".

WHAT IT PINS. (a) $C1C1's DEC -- without it the shield never runs out, $C1D6 never fires and the 121 dying frames go to 0. (b) $C1D0, destroy-what-you-hit: the enemy the shield absorbed is KILLED, so the enemy slots and the score move on every absorption, and a port that only DECs leaves the same enemy inside the box next frame and drains all five in five consecutive frames instead of over 154. The kills are load-bearing further on, too: they clear a squadron, and $47 steps 0 -> 1 at f561 -- a capsule promoted by a shield absorption. (c) the force field in OAM: an extra $8AAC on every shielded frame, which re-orders every sprite after it and moves three compared work counters. (d) $8B79's $9E = 3 flash on the 105 frames $46 == 1, which reads 0 at $80B5 in every run ever made and is therefore only ever visible through the picture.

scenarios.name: capsule-die
scenarios.why:
THE SEVENTH CAPSULE, THE RAPID-FIRE BONUS, AND THE DEATH WIPE. $42 is poked to 6 while a laser run is dropping capsules, so the cartridge's own next pickup INCs it to 7 and takes the $CE89 arm; the score there has ($07E5 & $0F) == 0, so $35 goes 20 -> 4.

MEASURED, this scenario's own artifact:
  f626  the poke lands: $42 0 -> 6, and it SITS there for nine frames (B is not held)
  f635  the pickup: $42 6 -> 1 (the wrap is to ONE, not zero), $35 20 -> 4,
        and $07E4/$07E5 take a kill's $0010 and the capsule's $0050 on one frame
  f676  $47 1 -> 2, a second squadron
  f690  a SECOND natural pickup, $42 1 -> 2, +$0050
  f793  $C1D6 -- the ship, now flying right, is killed by an enemy
  f914  $979D/$9B3E: $35 4 -> 20, $47 2 -> 0, $44 1 -> 0, $22 0 -> 1,
        and $42 2 -> 1 -- RESTORED from $22,X, not kept
121 dying frames. $8960 (the ($07E5 & $0F) == 5 score bonus) runs ZERO times here, which is the negative half of the same test.

FOUR THINGS ONLY THIS SCENARIO HOLDS. (1) The wrap: $42 goes to 1, not 0, and a port that wrapped to 0 is red on w_0042 from f635 to the end. (2) The rapid-fire bonus is a COMPARED CONSEQUENCE and not just w_0035: $35 is the autofire reload, so from f636 the shot cadence changes and w_03A3-w_03A8 and the whole of w_0123-w_012B move with it. (3) $8969's +$0050 runs on BOTH pickups. (4) The death wipe: $35 is NOT kept, it is overwritten by $9B5E's constant $14, and $42 is not kept either -- it comes back from $22,X, which $97AB set to ($42 ? 1 : 0), so a meter on cell 2 respawns on cell 1.

THE $44 POKE IS HELD, and what that costs is one frame rather than the whole respawn: $9B3E's wipe of $44 IS visible at f914 (1 -> 0) because the poke is applied after the sample, and f915 puts it back. Said here rather than left to be found.

scenarios.name: missile-wall-miss
scenarios.why:
THE CONTROL FOR `missile-wall`, and it is the reason that scenario is worth anything. Identical script, identical poke frame, and ONLY THE SECOND CELL poked: $05F6 = $10 without $05EE = $40. The missile's FIRST probe then reads 0, $A187's BEQ skips the whole discrimination, and the missile takes its ordinary fly step into the $A1B9 floor test -- so this window must be byte-identical to `autofire-missile` on w_0329 and everywhere else the missile shows. 

Without it, `missile-wall` proves only that poking SOMETHING changes SOMETHING. With it, the pair says the change comes from field 3 of $05EE and from nothing else. It also holds the other half of the arm: a port that took the wall branch on the first probe alone -- ignoring $A18B entirely -- is red HERE and green on `missile-wall`. 

The one thing both scenarios share is the shot slots: at $3E = 149 a shot at x in [83, 90] sits over $05F6's column and is absorbed by $C2E8. That is ported ($C0BD's three stores) and it happens identically in both, which is what makes it a shared control rather than a confound.
